sections.title: PhD Dissertation (defended 4 September 2026)
content: "Painful temporomandibular disorders and headache in young adulthood: early-life factors and multidimensional clinical characterization," Aarhus University.

The dissertation examined whether early-life factors (adolescent dietary quality and prenatal nutrition) are associated with painful temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and headache in young adulthood, and characterized the pain, psychosocial, somatosensory, and lifestyle profile of young adults with painful TMD, using data from the Danish National Birth Cohort.

sections.title: Current Postdoctoral Research: Life-Course and Epigenetic Analyses of Painful Temporomandibular Disorders
content: This postdoctoral project is a direct continuation of Mojdeh's PhD work. Its overall aim is to investigate epigenetic mechanisms underlying vulnerability to p-TMD, building on the epidemiological and clinical findings from her PhD within the Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC).

The project uses genome-wide DNA methylation profiling (Illumina EPIC arrays) on biological samples and clinical phenotyping data collected during the PhD, to identify epigenetic markers associated with p-TMD and examine whether fetal exposure, childhood diet, and adolescent lifestyle factors relate to differential DNA methylation patterns.
It is carried out in collaboration with Professor Lene Baad-Hansen (Aarhus University), Associate Professor Bodil Hammer Bech (Aarhus University), and Professor Luda Diatchenko (McGill University).

sections.title: Additional Research
content: Beyond her PhD dissertation, Mojdeh has contributed to several related research projects in recent years, spanning collaborative cohort studies, experimental pain research, and clinical qualitative work.

Exposto CR, Mansoori M, Bech BH, Baad-Hansen L. Prevalence of painful temporomandibular disorders and overlapping primary headaches among young adults. European Journal of Pain, 2025. A collaborative analysis of Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC) data examining how often p-TMD and primary headaches co-occur in young adulthood.

Exposto CR, Mansoori M, Bech BH, Bjerregaard AA, Olsen SF, Baad-Hansen L. Pre-natal nutrition as risk factor for painful temporomandibular disorders and headaches in young adults. Headache: The Journal of Head and Face Pain, 2025. A further DNBC collaboration investigating whether nutrition during pregnancy is associated with p-TMD and headache in the offspring as young adults.

Ghorbanizadeh S, Abbasnejad M, Zamyad M, Esmaeili-Mahani S, Kheirandish R, Mansoori M. Impact of temporomandibular disorder on food preference behavior in adult male rats. Archives of Oral Biology, 2025. An experimental study on how TMD-related pain affects feeding and food preference behavior.

Eghbali H, Abbasnejad M, Raoof M, Zamyad M, Esmaeili-Mahani S, Kooshki R, Mansoori M, Lobbezoo F. Alpha-pinene modulates feeding behavior and hypothalamic orexin-A expression in a rat model of painful temporomandibular disorder. Journal of Oral Facial Pain and Headache, 2026. A follow-up experimental study testing whether alpha-pinene can restore feeding behavior and orexin-A expression disrupted by TMD-related pain.

Raoof M, Fereidooni R, Afzali M, Mansoori M, Amanpour S, Rad M. Exploring the Etiology of Dental Fear Among Candidates for Endodontic Treatment: A Qualitative Investigation. Tanzania Journal of Health Research, 2025. A qualitative study of the reasons behind dental fear among patients undergoing endodontic treatment.
